title: Where to Stay in Fažana in 2027: Areas, Hotels & Rentals
metaDescription: A complete guide to Fažana neighborhoods, comparing Old Town hotels, North Fažana apartments, South resorts, and inland villas with 2027 prices and distances.
content:
## Fažana Old Town and Harbor (Best for Dining and Ferry Access)

The Old Town is the historical and commercial center of Fažana. Located directly on the waterfront, this compact, pedestrian-only zone is defined by narrow cobblestone streets, colorful townhouses, and the Trg Sv. Kuzme i Damjana (the main square). Staying here places visitors within 200 meters of the Brijuni National Park ferry departure point, making it highly practical for those prioritizing island excursions.

Accommodation in the center consists primarily of restored heritage hotels and boutique apartments above ground-floor businesses. Properties like Heritage Hotel Chersin and Villetta Phasiana offer high-standard rooms ranging from €130 to €170 per night during the summer season. Self-catering apartments in this zone typically cost between €90 and €140 per night.

Seafront properties along the harbor charge a premium for the view, but the constant noise from early morning ferry crowds and late-night restaurant clearing makes them a poor choice for light sleepers. The waterfront promenade stays active until well past midnight in July and August. Visitors seeking quiet should avoid rooms facing the main Riva (promenade) and instead look for accommodations facing the inner courtyards or back streets.

Parking is a significant logistical factor when staying in the Old Town. Because vehicles are prohibited in the historical center, visitors must park in designated public lots on the perimeter. The main public parking areas (such as Parking Badel or the large northern lot) charge around €1.50 per hour or up to €15 per day during the peak season. Hotels often provide dedicated spots or valet services, but independent apartment renters will need to budget for public parking and walk 300 to 500 meters to their rental with luggage.

### Supermarkets and Amenities in the Center
Those staying in the Old Town rely on smaller convenience stores for self-catering. The local Studenac market on the waterfront and nearby bakeries (pekaras) supply basic groceries, fresh bread, and local produce. For larger grocery runs, visitors will need to drive or walk 15 minutes to the larger supermarkets located on the town's outer edges.

## North Fažana / Sjever (Best for Quiet Beach Holidays)

The area immediately north of the Old Town, leading toward the Pineta camping grounds, is a residential and tourist zone characterized by pine forests and quiet streets. This neighborhood is centered around Ulica Pineta and Ulica ruža. It is an excellent area for families and older travelers who want easy beach access without the dense crowds of the center.

Accommodations here are predominantly low-rise apartment blocks and private houses offering floors or individual units for rent. Nightly rates for a standard one-bedroom apartment range from €80 to €120. Most properties in North Fažana are within a 100 to 400-meter walk to Dječje Igralište beach and San Lorenzo beach. These beaches feature fine pebbles, shallow entries into the Adriatic Sea, and natural shade provided by mature pine trees right up to the shoreline.

Walking from North Fažana to the Old Town harbor takes 10 to 15 minutes (approximately 800 meters) via a flat, paved seaside promenade. This makes it easy to access the restaurants and evening events in the center while sleeping in a much quieter environment.

Parking in North Fažana is straightforward. Almost all apartment rentals and private villas in this area include secure, off-street parking on the property. This eliminates the daily parking fees associated with the Old Town and makes North Fažana a practical base for travelers planning to use a rental car for day trips to Rovinj, Motovun, or Pula.

## South Fažana / Valbandon Border (Best for Resort Amenities)

South Fažana stretches from the Badel parking area down toward the neighboring village of Valbandon. This area is dominated by the Bi Village Holiday Center, a massive four-star resort complex, alongside modern apartment buildings and vacation homes.

Staying in the South Fažana zone is ideal for travelers who want active holidays and robust infrastructure. The shoreline here is defined by Bi Val beach, a long stretch of white pebbles equipped with sunbed rentals, water wibits (inflatable obstacle courses), parasailing, and beach bars. 

Accommodation within the Bi Village resort includes mobile homes, standard apartments, and camping pitches. A mobile home for a family of four typically costs between €150 and €220 per night in July and August. These rentals include access to the resort's three freshwater pools, evening animation programs, and sports courts.

Independent apartments situated just outside the resort on streets like Ulica Dragonja or Ulica Galižanska provide a middle ground. These private rentals average €90 to €130 per night. Visitors staying outside the resort can still use Bi Val beach (which is public), but accessing the resort's internal pools and private entertainment requires paying for a day visitor pass.

The walk from South Fažana to the Old Town takes 15 to 25 minutes depending on the exact location, covering a distance of 1 to 2 kilometers. The route follows the continuous coastal path. Cyclists often prefer this southern section because it connects seamlessly to the paved biking trails leading toward Štinjan and Pula.

### Grocery Access in South Fažana
South Fažana is highly convenient for self-catering due to the large Plodine supermarket situated directly on the main D75 road. This modern supermarket offers extensive fresh produce, a butcher, and a bakery, making it easy to stock up on supplies without navigating the narrow central streets.

## Inland Fažana / Upper Residential Zone (Best for Value and Private Villas)

The inland area of Fažana sits on the slight incline east of the main D75 bypass road, heading toward the village of Galižana. This zone is strictly residential, featuring larger plots of land, olive groves, and a high concentration of newly built holiday villas with private pools.

This area offers the best value per square meter. A private three-bedroom villa with a pool and sea views from the upper terrace typically costs between €250 and €400 per night, which is significantly cheaper than comparable properties directly on the coast. Standard apartments in this elevated zone drop to €60 to €90 per night.

The primary trade-off for the lower price and increased privacy is the distance to the sea. The shoreline and Old Town are 1 to 1.5 kilometers away. Walking down to the beach takes 15 to 20 minutes, and the return journey involves an uphill climb. Many visitors staying in the inland zone choose to drive to the beach, which means factoring in daily parking fees at the coastal lots.

However, for travelers prioritizing a quiet retreat, private swimming facilities, and easy road access to the rest of the Istrian peninsula, Inland Fažana is a highly practical choice. It completely avoids the summer traffic bottlenecks that occur near the harbor and resort entrances.

## Accessibility and Terrain

Fažana is generally very flat along the coastline, making the Old Town, North Fažana, and South Fažana highly accessible for wheelchair users, strollers, and travelers with limited mobility. The seafront promenade (Lungomare) is fully paved and lacks steep gradients for the entire 3-kilometer stretch from Pineta in the north to Bi Val in the south.

Inland Fažana is the only area that presents mobility challenges due to its elevation. The roads leading up from the D75 highway (such as Vodnjanska cesta) have moderate to steep inclines and often lack continuous sidewalks, requiring pedestrians to walk on the shoulder of the road.

## Seasonal Accommodation Availability

Fažana operates on a strict seasonal timeline. The primary tourist season runs from late May to late September. During July and August, occupancy rates frequently hit 95%, and last-minute bookings are rare and expensive. Travelers planning to visit during the local Pilchard Festival (usually held in August) should book their Old Town accommodations at least six months in advance.

Outside of the summer window, Fažana becomes a quiet residential town. By November, the large resorts in South Fažana close completely, and only a fraction of the private apartments remain available. The heritage hotels in the Old Town often stay open year-round, dropping their rates to €80 to €100 per night. Staying in the center is highly recommended during the winter and early spring, as the peripheral neighborhoods offer no open amenities.

faq.question: Do I need a car if I stay in Fažana?
faq.answer: You do not need a car if you stay in the Old Town, North Fažana, or South Fažana, as beaches, supermarkets, and restaurants are within a 20-minute walk. However, a car is highly recommended if you stay in Inland Fažana or plan to explore the wider Istrian peninsula.

faq.question: Which Fažana area is best for visiting Brijuni National Park?
faq.answer: The Old Town is the best area for visiting Brijuni National Park. The main ferry terminal and ticket office are located directly on the Fažana harbor promenade, making it a 2- to 5-minute walk from any accommodation in the center.

faq.question: Are the beaches in Fažana sandy?
faq.answer: No, there are no natural sandy beaches in Fažana. The coastline consists entirely of fine white pebbles and paved sunbathing terraces. Water shoes are recommended for comfort when entering the sea.

faq.question: Where is the best place to park in Fažana?
faq.answer: If your accommodation does not provide parking, the largest and most accessible public lots are Parking Badel (south of the center) and the large municipal lot next to the Plodine supermarket. Expect to pay up to €15 per day during July and August.

faq.question: Is Fažana suitable for families with young children?
faq.answer: Yes, Fažana is highly suitable for families. North Fažana offers shallow, pebble beaches with natural pine shade, while South Fažana provides extensive resort facilities, playgrounds, and inflatable water parks directly on the beach.

faq.question: Is the Fažana promenade accessible for wheelchairs and strollers?
faq.answer: Yes, the entire coastal promenade running through North Fažana, the Old Town, and South Fažana is flat, wide, and fully paved. It is highly accessible for both wheelchairs and strollers.

quickAnswer: Fažana is divided into four main areas. The pedestrian-only Old Town is ideal for dining and Brijuni ferries. North Fažana offers quieter, family-focused beaches. South Fažana provides large resort amenities at Bi Val beach. Inland Fažana features budget-friendly villas requiring a 10-15 minute walk to the coast.
